subject: A brief history of AI executives calling for regulation
posts: Tech executives keep sounding alarm bells about AI doom and calling for regulation, but history shows few meaningful guardrails have emerged. Evidence: CEO warnings, EO shifts, lobbying #AI #Policy
Tech leaders claim they want proactive federal regulation and legal guardrails to prevent existential harm from runaway artificial intelligence. Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Good Preference

Public warnings serve as a smart selfish maneuver to secure regulatory moats, locking out smaller competitors while incumbents retain unfettered deployment power. Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Calls for regulation mask incumbent moat-building behind manufactured existential pretexts.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 5.5, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Tech Executive Warnings: FAIL (-0.7, -0.6) — Regulatory capture and moat building.
- Government Response: COND (-0.2, -0.3) — Partisan gridlock and policy vacuum.
Despite decades of warnings from computer pioneers and modern tech CEOs about AI risks, federal policymaking remains paralyzed by partisanship and lobbying influence.

The Poison:
Framing commercial competition as an existential safety crisis shifts regulatory burdens onto open-source innovators while cementing monopolies.
The Plane Error mistakes commercial risk control (WHAT) for moral stewardship (WHO). Incumbents use safety pretexts to erect barriers against nimble startups.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors run a Smart Selfish maneuver: deploying manufactured existential anxiety (pretext) to lobby for rules that protect incumbent market dominance (power hoarding).

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map stated safety altruism against actual market capture, it plots toward Lesser Evil. Power concentrates via regulatory capture.

The Unavoidable Truth: Incumbents love regulation that keeps new rivals out of the market.

The Unavoidable Lie: Tech executives are lobbying for safety out of pure altruism.
